chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us from Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqdah, who reported from Ja'far ibn Abdullah, who reported from Sa'dan ibn Sa'id, who reported from Sufyan ibn Ibrahim al-Ghamidi al-Qadhi, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) saying:

Tests and trials begin with us and then with you, and the times of ease begin with us and then with you. And by the One by Whom oaths are taken, Allah shall surely triumph through you, just as He triumphed through the stones.

key_terms.البلاء: Trial, affliction, tribulation - referring to the sufferings endured by the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers
key_terms.الحجارة: Stones - referring to the stones of baked clay (sijjil) mentioned in Surah al-Fil (105:3-4) that destroyed the army of Abraha
key_terms.الرخاء: Ease, prosperity - the periods of relief that also begin with the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about trials and ease beginning with the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) taught his followers that the Ahl al-Bayt are the first to face tribulations and the first to experience ease, and that their followers (Shi'a) share in this pattern. He then swore an oath that God would grant victory through the Shi'a, comparing it to how He defeated the army of Abraha through the stones of baked clay (Surah al-Fil). This teaching was delivered in the context of consoling the Shi'a community during times of persecution under Umayyad and early Abbasid rule.
